note: The public version ladder: every released version, oldest first, each with a CHANGELOG.md section of its own (scripts/site.test.mjs). `summary` is written for the site. States: done, planned, goal, later. What comes after the current release is planned privately and is not listed until it ships.

rungs.summary: The foundation: the desktop app's shell over its own engine, the build checks on Windows, macOS and Linux, and this site.
Capture: screens, windows and webcams on Windows, macOS and Linux, live in the preview.
The GPU compositor: scenes built from sources and composed on the graphics card, with filters such as chroma key, color correction, LUTs and blur.
Audio and recording: a mixer with up to six tracks and classic-DSP filters, and multi-track recording with hardware encoders and Capture's own lossless format.
A native GPU preview: the program painted straight from the compositor, with no lag.
The studio: streaming to Twitch, YouTube, Kick, Facebook and Trovo with automatic reconnects, Studio Mode with transitions, hotkeys, profiles and a stats dock.
Streaming depth: multistream to several platforms at once, SRT and WHIP, a vertical canvas, nested scenes, a replay buffer and a chat overlay that needs no sign-in.
Remote control and extensions: a password-protected WebSocket API, browser docks, sandboxed Lua scripting and a plugin SDK, all local and off by default.
Distribution: a signed auto-updater, audio captured per application, and the licence agreement on first run.
A studio for everyone: 18 languages, full keyboard and screen-reader support, a first-run setup wizard, a command palette and themes.
Scene authoring and monitoring: undo and redo, an OBS scene-collection importer, alignment guides, a keying workbench, a multiview and projectors.
Broadcast safety: a go-live pre-flight, alarms, a source-health dashboard, encoder failover, crash-safe recording, a panic button and a quit guard.
Sources, devices and calibration: test signals, A/V sync calibration, timers and clocks, text from a file, a hotkey map, deinterlacing and camera controls.
Automation and capture depth: rules, macros, MIDI and OSC control, a LAN touch panel, tally lights, PTZ cameras and a show rundown, plus punch-in zoom and HDR-to-SDR tone-mapping.
New sources and overlays: instant replay, a gapless playlist, a title and scoreboard designer, an audio visualizer, a stats overlay, a split timer, an input overlay, LAN ingest and Freally Link.
Compositor depth: 3D corner-pin, downstream keyers, freeze-frame, more blurs, the move transition, a WGSL shader studio, bezier masks and track-matte stingers.
Audio production: output routing, a ducking matrix, an auto-mixer, loudness normalization, a parametric EQ, a soundboard, podcast recording and CLAP and VST3 plugin discovery.
Recording and replay depth: per-source ISO recording, a clip trimmer, recording with transparency, automatic markers, a post-record pipeline, an integrity check and SMPTE timecode.
Streaming insight: a network simulator, a rehearsal mode, a dropped-frame timeline, a session report, an encoder benchmark, and sources shown only on the stream or only in the recording.
Remote guests and show production: up to eight guests, a green room, cues, a connection-quality dashboard, a telestrator, a teleprompter and automatic guest grids.
Studio management: scene packs, compare and merge, named snapshots, portable mode, one-file backups, a theme editor and dock layouts.
The teleprompter, reworked: pause chips, a start countdown, BPM pacing, read-aloud, and autocomplete in all 18 languages.
The first stable release: every planned feature, plus a Starting Soon countdown, background music, a social bar and a featured chat banner.
A shareable MP4, written beside each lossless recording when it stops.
Deep capture and the web: a virtual camera, a true browser source and game capture, Windows first.
The audit: no new features, a full security and correctness pass, and the three 1.2.0 additions made to work.
